title: Relief on the Commitment Shortfall of a Closing Corporate Catering Service Agreement
content:
A client who came close to the commitment and kept ordering through the year is not asked for the whole of the shortfall. How much of the shortfall on a closing Corporate Catering Service Agreement falls due turns on the spend counted, measured against the minimum tested against, and on the number of invoiced orders the agreement carried in the 12 months ending on the day it closes.

1. Where the spend counted reaches three quarters — 0.75, that is 75 per cent — of the minimum tested against, taken to two decimal places, and the agreement carried 3 or more invoiced orders in the 12 months ending on the day it closes, none of the shortfall falls due: the share due is 0 per cent.
2. Where the spend counted reaches half — 0.5, that is 50 per cent — of the minimum tested against, taken to two decimal places, and the agreement carried 3 or more invoiced orders in that window, half of the shortfall falls due: the share due is 50 per cent.
3. Otherwise the whole of the shortfall falls due: the share due is 100 per cent.

### Both sides of the thresholds

Take a hypothetical closing agreement whose minimum tested against is 40000.00 USD, so that three quarters of it is 30000.00 USD and half of it is 20000.00 USD.

| Spend counted | Invoiced orders in that window | Share of the shortfall that falls due |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 30000.00 USD | 3 | 0 per cent |
| 29999.99 USD | 3 | 50 per cent |
| 20000.00 USD | 5 | 50 per cent |
| 19999.99 USD | 5 | 100 per cent |
| 32000.00 USD | 2 | 100 per cent |

The order count is tested on both of the relieving branches, so an agreement carrying 2 invoiced orders in that window is on the third branch however high its spend counted stands. An agreement carrying exactly 3 invoiced orders meets the count on either branch.
